title: Causa Limena
subtitle: peruvian chilled potato terrine
excerpt: A Peruvian chilled terrine of mashed potato layered with a savoury chicken filling. The lime and chilli in the potato are the signature touch. Served cold.
sourceNotes: Causa Limena is one of Lima's most iconic dishes. Yellow potato is traditional, but any waxy variety works. It is assembled in a terrine mould or individual rings and served chilled.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the causa up to 8 hours ahead and refrigerate, covered, until needed.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Peruvian dish of mashed potato layered with savoury fillings, served chilled.

content.text: is layered together cold. The potato is mashed with olive oil, lime and chilli until it becomes smooth, pliable and sharp. It is pressed into a mould, filled with a simple chicken and yoghurt mixture, and topped with another potato layer.
The potato must be completely smooth before assembling. Any lumps will stop the layers holding together cleanly when sliced.
Boil the potatoes in unsalted water until completely tender, about 20 minutes. Drain well and leave to steam-dry for 5 minutes.

Pass the potato through a food processor or mash by hand until completely smooth. Stir in the lime juice, minced chilli and olive oil while still warm. The potato should taste sharp and a little spicy. Season to taste and set aside to cool completely.
Mix the shredded chicken with the yoghurt, diced onion and coriander in a bowl. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Line a small loaf tin or four individual rings with cling film. Press half the potato mixture into the base, smoothing it to an even layer about 2 cm thick. Spoon the chicken filling over evenly. Top with the remaining potato and press down firmly.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Turn out onto a plate to serve. Slice with a sharp knife dipped in water to get clean portions.

attrs.issue: Potato layer is crumbling when sliced

content.text: The potato needs more oil to bind it. Add another tablespoon of olive oil and work it in thoroughly. Make sure the potato is fully cooled before slicing.
Add more lime juice and increase the chilli. The potato should taste assertively sour and spicy on its own, as the filling is mild.

attrs.issue: Filling is too wet and leaks from the layers

content.text: Squeeze the shredded chicken dry before mixing. Use thick yoghurt rather than runny. Leave the assembled causa in the fridge for longer to firm up.

Causa is named after the Quechua word for force or power. It was eaten as a sustaining food during times of hardship. Lima has its own version, Causa Limena, which became the most well-known. Peruvians make it for birthdays, parties, and Sunday lunches. Yellow potato is the traditional base because it has a denser texture than white varieties. Today it appears in upscale Lima restaurants as an elegant starter.
